newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa delays Sun Air bid shortlist announcement.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa delays Sun Air bid shortlist announcement.

text.p: The South African government said on Wednesday that it had postponed the announcement of pre-qualifiers bidding for internal airline Sun Air to resolve a potential conflict of interest.

"The announcement has been delayed for a few days to work out a means of resolving a potential conflict of interest that has arisen in the restructuring process," the Transport and Public Enterprise Ministries said in a joint statement.
The conflict of interest had arisen from the fact that one of the consortiums seeking pre-qualification to tender had one of its related structures participating in the privatisation process.
A meeting would be held on Monday, April 21, to discuss the matter.
The statement added that the postponement was unlikely to affect the conclusion of what had been a "successful project".
A Public Enterprises spokesman said no further details were available at this stage.
The government is selling 100 percent of the Sun Air, formerly the carrier for the nominally independent homeland of Bophuthatswana, as part of its privatisation drive.
The sale will comprise three stages -- pre-qualification, submission of non-binding offers and final offers/completion.
Richard Branson's Virgin group is among those to have expressed an interest in acquiring the airline.
More than 10 bids for the airline had been received by merchant bank BOE NatWest and legal adviser Moseneke & Partners who are handling the sale.
